text:
Consider a solid sphere of radius R and mass
density
 $ρ(r)=ρ_{0}\left (1-\frac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}\right )$ , $0<r\leq R$
 The
minimum density of a liquid in which it will
float is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The mass of the sphere is found by summing thin shells of radius $r$ and thickness $dr$:


[IMG]

$M=\int\limits _{0}^{R}ρ_{0}\left (1-\dfrac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}\right )4πr^{2}dr=4πρ_{0}\left [\dfrac{R^{3}}{3}-\dfrac{1}{R^{2}}\cdot \dfrac{R^{5}}{5}\right ]=4πρ_{0}\cdot \dfrac{2R^{3}}{15}=\dfrac{8πρ_{0}R^{3}}{15}$

The sphere floats only if the buoyant force when fully immersed is at least its weight; the minimum density $ρ_{l}$ of the liquid makes them equal:

$ρ_{l}\cdot \dfrac{4}{3}πR^{3}g=\dfrac{8πρ_{0}R^{3}}{15}g\Rightarrow ρ_{l}=\dfrac{8}{15}\times \dfrac{3}{4}ρ_{0}=\dfrac{2ρ_{0}}{5}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
When photon of energy 4.0 eV strikes the
surface of a metal A, the ejected photoelectrons
have maximum kinetic energy $T_{A} eV$ and
de-Broglie wavelength $λ_{A}$. The maximum
kinetic energy of photoelectrons liberated from
another metal B by photon of energy 4.50 eV
is $T_{B} = (T_{A} – 1.5) eV$. If the de-Broglie
wavelength of these photoelectrons $λ_{B}$ = 2$λ_{A}$,
then the work function of metal B is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, de-Broglie wavelength

$λ$ = $\frac{h}{p}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK_{e}}}$

$\therefore$ $λ\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{K_{e}}}$

So $\frac{λ_{A}}{λ_{B}}=\sqrt{\frac{T_{B}}{T_{A}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}$ = $\frac{T_{A}-1.5}{T_{A}}$

On solving $T_{A} = 2 eV$

$\therefore$ $T_{B} = T_{A} - 1.5 = 0.5 eV$

Also $T_{B} = 4.5 -$ $𝜙_{B}$

$\Rightarrow$ 0.5 = 4.5 - $𝜙_{B}$

$\Rightarrow$ $𝜙_{B}$ = 4 eV
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

$\Rightarrow$ B = 0.71 mT

text:
In finding the electric field using Gauss Law
the formula $\left |\vec{E}\right |=\frac{q_{enc}}{ε_{0}|A|}$ is applicable. In the
formula $ε_{0}$ is permittivity of free space, A is the
area of Gaussian surface and $q_{$enc} is charge
enclosed by the Gaussian surface. The equation
can be used in which of the following situation?
options: Only when $\left |\vec{E}\right |$ = constant on the surface.
For any choice of Gaussian surface.

Only when the Gaussian surface is an
equipotential surface.

Only when the Gaussian surface is an
equipotential surface and $\left |\vec{E}\right |$ is constant on
the surface.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By Gauss law

$\int \vec{E}.d\vec{A}=\frac{q_{in}}{ε_{0}}$

When $\vec{E}||\vec{A}$ and $\left |\vec{E}\right |$ is constant then

$E\int dA=\frac{q_{in}}{ε_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$EA = $\frac{q_{in}}{ε_{0}}$

$\therefore$ $\left |\vec{E}\right |$ should be constant on the surface and the
surface should be equipotential.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
A body A, of mass m = 0.1 kg has an initial
velocity of 3$\hat{i}$ $ms^{-1}$ . It collides elastically with
another body, B of the same mass which has
an initial velocity of 5$\hat{j}$ $ms^{-1}$. After collision,
A moves with a velocity $\vec{v}=4\left (\hat{i}+\hat{j}\right )$. The
energy of B after collision is written as $\frac{x}{10}$. The value of x is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By conservation of linear momentum :

(0.1)(3$\hat{i}$) + (0.1)(5$\hat{j}$) = (0.1)(4)($\hat{i}$ + $\hat{j}$) + (0.1)$\vec{v}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{v}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}$

$\therefore$ $\left |\vec{v}\right |$ = $\sqrt{2}$

$KE_{B} =$ $\frac{1}{2}\times 0.1\times \left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{2}$ = $\frac{1}{10}$ J

$\therefore$ x = 1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
A particle is moving along the x-axis with its
coordinate with the time 't' given be
 $x(t) = 10 + 8t – 3t^{2}$. Another particle is moving
the y-axis with its coordinate as a function of
time given by $y(t) = 5 – 8t^{3}$. 
At t = 1s, the speed
of the second particle as measured in the frame
of the first particle is given as $\sqrt{v}$. Then v
(in m/s) is $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a particle ‘A’, its position along the x-axis as a function of time $t$ is given by:

$x(t)=10+8t-3t^{2}$

To find the velocity $v_{A}$, we take the derivative of $x(t)$ with respect to $t$:

$v_{A}=\frac{d}{dt}[10+8t-3t^{2}]=8-6t$

At $t=1$ second, the velocity of particle A is:

$⃗{v_{A}}=(8-6\cdot 1)\hat{i}=2\hat{i}$

For a particle ‘B’, its position along the y-axis as a function of time $t$ is given by:

$y(t)=5-8t^{3}$

To find the velocity $v_{B}$, we take the derivative of $y(t)$ with respect to $t$:

$v_{B}=\frac{d}{dt}[5-8t^{3}]=-24t^{2}$

At $t=1$ second, the velocity of particle B is:

$⃗{v_{B}}=-24\cdot 1^{2}\hat{j}=-24\hat{j}$

The velocity of particle B relative to particle A ($⃗{v_{B/A}}$) is calculated as:

$⃗{v_{B/A}}=⃗{v_{B}}-⃗{v_{A}}$

$⃗{v_{B/A}}=-24\hat{j}-2\hat{i}$

To find the magnitude of $⃗{v_{B/A}}$:

$|⃗{v_{B/A}}|=\sqrt{(-24)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}=\sqrt{576+4}=\sqrt{580}$

Therefore, $v$ is:

$v=580$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
A one metre long (both ends open) organ pipe
is kept in a gas that has double the density of
air at STP. Assuming the speed of sound in air
at STP is 300 m/s, the frequency difference
between the fundamental and second harmonic
of this pipe is $________ Hz$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Velocity of sound v = $\sqrt{\frac{B}{ρ}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{v_{pipe}}{v_{air}}=\sqrt{\frac{\frac{B}{2ρ}}{\frac{B}{ρ}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{$pipe} = $\frac{v_{air}}{\sqrt{2}}$ = $\frac{300}{\sqrt{2}}$ = 150$\sqrt{2}$

We know, for open organ pipe

$f_{n} =$ $(n+1)\frac{v_{pipe}}{2l}$

Difference between $2^{nd}$ and fundamental frequency

$f_{1} - f_{0} =$ $\frac{v_{pipe}}{2l}$ = $\frac{150\sqrt{2}}{2(1)}$ = 106.06 Hz
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot
